guard: attach redeems an open mesh's session grant with no local seed, a sealed mesh still refuses an unseeded redeem BY NAME against a live broker, the redeem link is chosen by the recorded mesh mode rather than by the presence of a credential, and neither arm invents or drops one
command: pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/workspace build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/cli build && pnpm smoke:attach-open-mode
why: Issue #1205: the session redeem required this space's LOCAL SEED, and an open-mode mesh has no
seed BY DESIGN, so attach refused exactly the configuration it exists to serve. The repair makes
the redeem contract a VALUE chosen by the recorded mesh mode (`RedeemLink`), not an inference
from a nullable credential. These mutations attack that claim from both directions.
THE MOST IMPORTANT CELL IS THE REFUSING ONE. A fix that makes the open case pass by relaxing the
seed check on SEALED meshes would leave the open cell green and break a sealed mesh silently.
MUTATION 4 and MUTATION 6 exist to prove that cell can still fail ON THE FIXED TREE: each
weakens the sealed arm in the exact way a band-aid would, and each must be KILLED by a cell that
names the sealed refusal against a LIVE authed broker.
MUTATION 1 restores the defect itself: the open arm is removed, so a seedless open target falls
through to the sealed test. The live open attach reds, because the binary prints the #1205
refusal instead of `attached to`.
MUTATION 2 is the defect in the other direction: a sealed mesh WITH its seed takes the bare path.
The mint cell reds. The live open attach still passes, so this mutation is discriminated by the
sealed cell alone, which is the point of having both.
MUTATION 3 restores the old operator copy, which told the operator to re-register a root the mesh
had already resolved. The remediation cell reds.
MUTATION 4 makes the SEALED arm fall back to the open path when the seed is absent - the precise
band-aid this brief forbids. The live sealed-refusal cell reds.
MUTATION 5 makes `redeemConnectOpts` synthesise a credential for a bare link. `standaloneConnectOpts`
then builds an authenticator for an open mesh, which is the 'invent a seed' failure mode. The
no-credential cell reds.
MUTATION 6 deletes the connect-time refusal that names a missing static seed as still authenticated.
Without it a credless probe classifies the mesh as open-now-wants-auth and the sealed cells red.
MUTATION 7 drops the recorded mode as it is carried out of the resolve, so the redeem decision
sees `undefined` for every mesh. Open meshes then take the sealed arm and the live open cell reds.
This is the seam a future caller would silently reintroduce the seed requirement through.
MUTATION 8 and MUTATION 9 cover the SIXTH seed reach, found in review rather than by the author:
attach resolves seat locality first (pinForTarget -> locateSeat -> scatterManager), and that site
still answers open-vs-sealed from the absence of a credential. It is safe because its answer only
selects whether liveness is PROBED, so the worst case is a not-probed row and never a refusal.
It is graded in BOTH directions anyway: 8 removes the bare arm, 9 reclassifies a seedless sealed
mesh as open at that site.

mutations.name: the #1205 defect restored: an open mesh again falls through to the seed requirement
mutations.replace:
case "open":
      return t.spaceAuth ? { kind: "mint", auth: t.spaceAuth } : { kind: "fatal", message: attachNoSeedMessage(t) };
mutations.note: The pre-fix attach treated a missing seed as fatal even when the registry said the mesh was open.

mutations.name: a sealed mesh's own seed is ignored and the redeem goes bare
mutations.find: return t.spaceAuth ? { kind: "mint", auth: t.spaceAuth } : { kind: "fatal", message: attachNoSeedMessage(t) };
mutations.expectRed: ACCEPT: a sealed mesh with its seed still mints from THAT seed
mutations.cell: ACCEPT: a sealed mesh with its seed still mints from THAT seed
mutations.note: The defect in the other direction: an authenticated mesh that holds its seed is redeemed as if it were open.

mutations.name: a missing sealed seed again tells the operator to re-register the already-resolved root
mutations.expectRed: REFUSE (same absent seed, mode `auth`): a sealed mesh still refuses, and names restore-at-checkout
mutations.cell: REFUSE (same absent seed, mode `auth`): a sealed mesh still refuses, and names restore-at-checkout
mutations.note: The copy issue #1205 called out: the remedy named a root the command had already resolved correctly.

mutations.name: THE BAND-AID: a sealed mesh with no seed is rescued by the open path
mutations.find:
default:
      return t.spaceAuth ? { kind: "mint", auth: t.spaceAuth } : { kind: "fatal", message: attachNoSeedMessage(t) };
mutations.replace:
default:
      return t.spaceAuth ? { kind: "mint", auth: t.spaceAuth } : { kind: "bare" };
mutations.expectRed: REFUSE (same absent seed, mode `auth`): a sealed mesh still refuses, and names restore-at-checkout
mutations.cell: REFUSE (same absent seed, mode `auth`): a sealed mesh still refuses, and names restore-at-checkout
mutations.note: This is the exact shape of a fix that makes #1205's open case pass by weakening the sealed one. MEASURED, and worth stating precisely because a reviewer challenged the original wording: applied ALONE it reddens the IN-PROCESS sealed-refusal cell, not the live one, because connectOrThrow's mode check (mutation 6's target) refuses the seedless sealed mesh one layer earlier and the live attach never reaches the redeem decision. Removing BOTH guards together reddens the LIVE sealed cell as well (re-measured on the current suite: 26 passed / 4 failed; the pass count moved when resolver cells were added, the 4 reds did not). So the sealed refusal is defended in depth by two independent guards, and each is killed by a cell that names it.

mutations.name: the bare redeem invents a credential for an open mesh
mutations.replace:
return standaloneConnectOpts({ creds: (link as { creds?: string }).creds ?? "-----BEGIN NATS USER JWT-----
synthesised
------END NATS USER JWT------
", tls: link.tls });
mutations.expectRed: a bare redeem carries NO credential: the fix does not invent or synthesise a seed for an open mesh
mutations.cell: a bare redeem carries NO credential: the fix does not invent or synthesise a seed for an open mesh
mutations.note: Synthesising a seed for an open mesh is the forbidden repair; the connect-options cell is what forbids it.

mutations.name: a registered sealed mesh with no seed is probed and connected as open
mutations.expectRed: connecting to a sealed mesh whose seed is gone refuses by name, and says the mesh is NOT open
mutations.cell: connecting to a sealed mesh whose seed is gone refuses by name, and says the mesh is NOT open
mutations.note: Without this refusal a credless probe classifies the mesh as open-now-wants-auth, and the sealed contract is decided by a probe rather than by the record.

mutations.name: the recorded mesh mode is dropped on its way to the redeem decision
mutations.note: The carry-forward seam. A future caller that forgets to propagate the recorded mode silently reintroduces the seed requirement on every open mesh, which is exactly issue #1205.

mutations.name: THE SIXTH REACH: an open mesh's scatter probe tries to mint instead of riding bare
mutations.expectRed: ACCEPT: an open mesh's scatter probes bare, minting nothing
mutations.cell: ACCEPT: an open mesh's scatter probes bare, minting nothing
mutations.note: The sixth seed reach on the attach path (attach -> pinForTarget -> locateSeat -> scatterManager). Losing the bare arm makes an open mesh fall through to the seed test at a site the redeem never sees.

mutations.name: THE SIXTH REACH, the dangerous direction: a sealed mesh with no seed REFUSES at the scatter
mutations.expectRed: REFUSE (same creds, seed absent): a sealed mesh keeps what it arrived with and DEGRADES, never refusing
mutations.cell: REFUSE (same creds, seed absent): a sealed mesh keeps what it arrived with and DEGRADES, never refusing
mutations.note: A sealed mesh with no seed must DEGRADE here, not be reclassified as open. Treating it as open at this site is the same class of error as #1205, one call before the redeem.

mutations.name: the mode the resolver SYNTHESISES is broken: an unregistered seedless root stops resolving as open
mutations.expectRed: ACCEPT: an UNREGISTERED root with no seed resolves to mode "open", not to an absent mode
mutations.cell: ACCEPT: an UNREGISTERED root with no seed resolves to mode "open", not to an absent mode
mutations.note: localTarget DERIVES the mode that the redeem decision then reads, so the resolver decides the redeem contract one step earlier. Mutating the derived mode to another VALID member (not undefined, which only breaks the build and proves nothing) shows the resolver cells actually observe that derivation rather than restating the hand-built case.
